messages:
Nina (oncall): :rotating_light: sfo1 metrics alert — 5xx spike and GPU queue depth rising since 06:12 UTC. Also seeing elevated KMS signer latency (~600-1200ms). Dashboards: https://grafana.internal/r/xyz
Omar (eng-sre): I’m on logs. Peering shows flaps to provider peer 10.64.73.2, lots of retransmits and TCP resets. Provider status page shows degraded BGP in SFO.
Priya (infra-lead): GPU nodes show normal health, but attach operations to volumes are timing out in some AZs — mounting errors: `i/o timeout` and `attach failed: rpc deadline exceeded`. Could be network to control plane or provider side.
Marcus (eng-runtime): Runtime sees KV cache churn and many KMS timeouts while decrypting model keys -> that amplifies latency per request. If KMS calls fail we stall token generation.
Sasha (security): Don’t fallback to plaintext keys. We can consider increasing local KMS signer caching TTL for sfo1 and using secondary KMS in eu-central as a signed fallback, but that’s cross-region — need approvals.
Omar (eng-sre): Immediate mitigations I propose: 1) shift 30% of traffic from sfo1 -> ord3 via smart routing policy, 2) increase kms-signing-cache TTL to 10m for sfo1 only, 3) scale ord3 GPU pool + enable burst capacity. Running commands now.
Priya (infra-lead): Starting scale: `infractl capacity scale --region ord3 --pool gpu-xlarge --replicas +12 --reason "sfo1 peering congestion"` — rolling out. ETA ~7m for nodes to register. Also opened ticket with cloud provider (INC-45219).
Marcus (eng-runtime): I can flip a canary config to enable `kms_local_cache=true` for sfo1 to reduce signer RPCs; cache still encrypted and TTL=300s. Needs ops go-ahead. That will reduce KMS dependency while provider BGP converges.
Sasha (security): Approve temporary `kms_local_cache=true` for sfo1 for up to 3 hours. Must log TTL and rotation ops, and ensure HSM-backed keys are used for cache encryption.
deploy-bot: Canary config applied to 6 hosts in sfo1: `runtime.kms_local_cache=true`, `runtime.kms_cache_ttl=300` — rollout id r-2026-03-18-014.
Omar (eng-sre): Reroute policy pushed: `routingctl set-policy --region sfo1 --shift 30% --targets ord3,ord1 --reason bpggap` — traffic metrics showing initial reduction in error volume.
support-bot: Alerting customers tagged as "high-sensitivity" who have traffic routed through sfo1. Draft msg ready for CS review.
Ava (customer-success): Sending notice to customers in the affected cohort now with mitigation summary and ETA for full recovery.
Omar (eng-sre): Quick numbers: error-rate sfo1 5xx down from 6.2% -> 2.1% in the last 4m after reroute + cache. GPU queue depth trending down. KMS latency p95 dropped to ~220ms.
Nina (oncall): Good. Keep monitoring. Action items: (1) Priya open provider escalation link and attach pcap/traces, (2) Marcus to capture post-change perf baselines, (3) Sasha to log security approval and rotate cache key after incident, (4) Ava to update customers.
Priya (infra-lead): Provider responded: partial peering degradation due to edge router CPU saturation; they’re rehoming sessions. ETA they gave ~50m for full stabilization.
Marcus (eng-runtime): We’ll keep `kms_local_cache` for sfo1 until provider stable, then revert and validate no regressions with canary. Plan to add automated fallback to cache TTL on similar network anomalies.
Sasha (security): After we revert, we must rotate the KMS cache encryption key and run an audit of exposures. I’ll prepare runbook steps.
Nina (oncall): Closing loop: creating a postmortem ticket and assign owners. Marking incident as "mitigated" but still monitoring for 2 hours. Will update when provider confirms fix. :thumbsup:
Omar (eng-sre): Logs and traces collected in the incident bundle: s3://redwood-incident-bundles/1939005678.tar.gz
support-bot: Notifying #status-updates channel with summary and link to bundle.
Nina (oncall): Thanks all — leave this thread open until provider confirms, otherwise we’ll revert routing after 2h and run the postmortem."
